title: Reduce repeated saved-output proof reconstruction
changes: Reuse identical initial-direct proof reconstruction within one saved-candidate read: a same-host retained-job benchmark fell from 14.88 to 2.53 seconds, with identical output. This is not whole-conversion or AI latency.
Place package downloads before long reports and collapse the complete omissions list behind an accessible count summary without removing details.
Allow up to 90 seconds for saved-package GET checks while retaining the existing 180-second preparation budget, source binding and no-automatic-retry behavior.
Generate and download a reviewed, offline-format-validated APEXlang ZIP without database import, browser tests or reimport as delivery gates.
Prepare a separate format-only package from an eligible saved design without repeating model calls or changing the original run and its failures.
Show declared compatibility, generated MMD, prerequisites, omissions and recorded AI-request timings in the workbench.
Remove duplicated OPAF setup requests and reuse a freshly pinned TLS connection within each prepared role call when the server supports keepalive.
Keep direct OCI and legacy OPAF evidence compatible, and give SQLcl batch scripts an explicit EOF input pipe.
limitations: Development preview: source and local checks do not establish a public deployment or completed fresh-customer installation.
Only explicitly approved redacted source may be processed by the selected provider.
Format validation is not customer-target import testing, runtime verification or business acceptance; no universal import or behavior guarantee is made.
Supported Oracle Forms tooling, Java and SQLcl remain external prerequisites. Export-only jobs reuse configured provider and compatibility metadata without a live target connection.
The primary new output is an APEXlang ZIP with synthetic supporting SQL and explicit omissions, not a conventional database-derived SQL export.
Measured local protocol-count reductions are not a claimed cloud-model speedup. Dependency-sensitive mapping remains serial; unknown model outcomes are never automatically repeated.
